sections.body: The sources repeatedly show that real-time graphics methods gain speed by accepting controlled approximation, then managing the artifacts that approximation creates.
sections.heading: Controlled approximation

sections.body: ReSTIR has biased and unbiased variants, including a candidate-PDF MIS correction for one bias source and visual risks near visibility, geometry, or shading discontinuities. Temporal reuse can accumulate blur or fail around disocclusions, while image-based crowd rendering and graph bundling manage popping, texture storage, overdraw, and direction distortion.
sections.heading: Artifact evidence

sections.body: This topic should emphasize evidence-backed trade-offs rather than treating artifacts as implementation details: approximation changes what information is preserved, what must be recomputed, and what users can reliably interpret.
sections.heading: Interpretation risk
